findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The reset time is parsed from reply text twice: once in the driver, then again from `detail` inside athena-core. This breaks 'recognised once in the driver layer and carried as a typed result'.
findings.evidence: Read claude.rs: `output_from_result` builds `detail` as `format!("{subtype}: {text}")` with the text cut to 300 characters. The plan has `parse_usage_limit` work out the reset Timestamp in that function, then throw it away. `invoke_and_record` later calls `usage_limit_reset(detail, ended_at)` to parse the formatted, truncated detail string a second time. So the core crate depends on the text layout of `detail`, and the value the driver already computed is lost. The only reason given is that athena-agent/src/lib.rs is not a listed deliverable. Yet the plan already goes outside the list for crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. And the root-cause default says to name an out-of-scope fix and make it, not work around it. Fix: Add one typed field to `AgentOutput` in crates/athena-agent/src/lib.rs, for example `limit_resets_at: Option<jiff::Timestamp>`. Set it in `claude::output_from_result` from the single `parse_usage_limit` call, and in fake.rs through the same function. Copy it straight onto `Invocation.limit_resets_at` in `invoking.invocation_record`/`invoke_and_record`. Drop `usage_limit_reset(detail, ..)`. List lib.rs as a needed extra file and say why: the root cause sits in the driver's output type.

findings.summary: docs/records.md documents the record fields and outcome values but is not updated for the new `limited` outcome and `limit_resets_at` field.
findings.evidence: Grep found `timed_out` documented in docs/records.md lines 131-136 as an invocation outcome, with notes on how old records are read. The plan adds `InvocationOutcome::Limited` and `Invocation.limit_resets_at` but changes no record docs. Fix: Add docs/records.md to the files. Document the `limited` outcome (cost reported 0, empty models_used, lower-bound tokens) and the optional `limit_resets_at` field, and note that older records load unchanged.
findings.location: Files list; docs/records.md (invocation record row and outcome text near lines 84-136)

findings.summary: The plan does not check whether any doc or policy test lists `InvocationOutcome` values or `Stop` labels outside the Rust code.
findings.evidence: The plan says it did not search for other places that list `Stop::ALL`. Outcome values are also listed in prose in docs/records.md and docs/enforcement.md (Grep for `timed_out`). Fix: In step 1, Grep docs/ and xtask/ for the existing stop labels (for example 'repeated failure') and for outcome names, and update every list found.

findings.summary: Writing the account-wide hold file inside `invoke_and_record` mixes recording with a side effect that only status reads.
findings.evidence: `invoke_and_record`'s doc says it runs one agent and mirrors its record to the state directory. The plan adds a second, global write there. Fix: Acceptable as planned. Optionally, put the hold write in a small `disk::record_usage_limit` helper called from that spot, and update the doc comment.

summary: Basis: I read claude.rs, fake.rs, stream.rs, reconcile.rs, invocation.rs, disk.rs and parts of tests/drain.rs and docs/records.md; I ran nothing. The plan's main claims hold. `output_from_result` (claude.rs:249) turns every non-success result into `Error`. `check_invocation` (reconcile.rs:56) skips the cost check when `models_used` is empty and the token check when tokens are not measured, so a zero-cost Limited record with lower-bound tokens passes the gate unchanged. `is_environment_reason`/`resumable_stop` (disk.rs:212-227) give an existing path that keeps the candidate and allows retry. `FakeTurn` and the claude.rs stand-in `MODE` script with its `driver(...)` helper exist. `ResultEvent` has public fields, so fake.rs can send its text through `output_from_result`. tests/drain.rs has the low-disk `RealSteps` tests the plan cites. The demonstrations exercise real stage entry points and would fail without the behaviour. Athena's finding on tests/drain.rs is fair, but the test-only extension is justified. The one major problem is soundness: the reset time is worked out in the driver, dropped, then parsed again from the formatted and truncated `detail` string in athena-core. That goes against the reading's 'recognised once, carried typed', and exists only to avoid a one-line lib.rs change. Carry it as a typed `AgentOutput` field instead. Smaller points: the record docs in docs/records.md need the new outcome and field, and the plan should search for doc lists of stop and outcome names.
